title: Accessibility latency hardening
description: Objective: enforce keyboard, screen-reader, monochrome, loading, degraded, narrow-window, and latency behavior across the standalone app. Deliverable: shared accessibility/performance harnesses and fixed components. NOT in scope: visual redesign outside the pinned spec. Hard dependencies: all canonical control-room surfaces. Owned paths: apps/control-room/src/a11y/**, apps/control-room/src/performance/**, and UI-wide acceptance fixtures. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test.
definitionOfDone: All actions and provenance affordances work without mouse or color.
Loading/degraded states never expose stale mutation and timing separates server, stream, render, and human time.
Specified render/interaction bars pass on the reference environment.
taskRails: The standalone control room displays daemon truth and nextAllowedCommands; it never derives authority, readiness, or evidence strength.
Every fact is text/icon/color encoded, keyboard accessible, provenance-drillable, and honest under degraded data.
IDE adapters remain thin optional launch/discover/embed shells with no product logic. Keep modules below 400 lines; explicit owned paths only.

Write down the exact set of keys already owned surface-locally: j, k, h, l, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Enter, p, Escape. The global router in step 3 must NOT claim any of them. No files are modified in this step.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red: write the failing spec for the section 11.2 global keyboard map as pure logic, before any implementation. Cover, as a table-driven sweep over every binding: the g-chord (g then g/b/r/t resolving to goals/board/graph/timeline), single keys a (approvals), / (search), ? (help overlay), [ and ] (collapse/expand inspector). Then cover the refusal paths, and assert the SPECIFIC stable reason code returned for each, never merely that no action resolved: focus inside a text entry (input, textarea, contenteditable) refuses with TEXT_ENTRY_FOCUSED so typing a goal title never navigates; a key already owned by a surface (j, k, h, l, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Enter, p, Escape) refuses with SURFACE_LOCAL; an unbound key refuses with NO_BINDING; the first key of the chord returns CHORD_PENDING; and a chord whose second key is not one of g/b/r/t refuses with CHORD_ABANDONED and clears the pending prefix rather than leaving it armed. Assert the sweep actually generated cases (a table length greater than zero, and every declared binding exercised exactly once) so a silently empty sweep cannot pass. Tests fail because the module does not exist yet.
implementationPlan.note: TDD RED recorded. Added non-vacuous table-driven coverage for all 9 global bindings, all 9 surface-local keys, three text-entry shapes, and exact refusal codes TEXT_ENTRY_FOCUSED, SURFACE_LOCAL, NO_BINDING, CHORD_PENDING, CHORD_ABANDONED including cleared chord state. Fresh focused invocation failed for the expected reason: Failed to resolve import './keyboard-map.js'; 25 pre-existing app test files / 369 tests remained green.

implementationPlan.description: Make step 2 green with the minimum implementation. Export CONTROL_ROOM_KEYBOARD_MAP as a frozen table of the section 11.2 bindings the router owns, the frozen SURFACE_LOCAL_KEYS set it must defer on, and a pure resolver returning a discriminated result: either {matched:true, action} or {matched:false, reason} where reason is one of the stable codes TEXT_ENTRY_FOCUSED, SURFACE_LOCAL, NO_BINDING, CHORD_PENDING, CHORD_ABANDONED. Chord state is a caller-held value passed in and returned, so the resolver stays pure and testable without a DOM. Add a useKeyboardRouter hook in the same module that attaches one document-level keydown listener, delegates every decision to the resolver, calls preventDefault only when a binding actually matched, and removes the listener on unmount so a remount cannot double-handle. The hook derives nothing: it never infers an action the map does not declare. Keep the module under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented a 142-line pure keyboard resolver plus document hook. The table and every nested binding/sequence are frozen; SURFACE_LOCAL_KEYS is an immutable ReadonlySet facade, not a mutable frozen Set. Resolver returns exact discriminated reason codes and caller-held chord state. Hook handles matched actions once, prevents defaults only on matches, and removes/reset its listener/state on cleanup. Added hook lifecycle/text/local/chord tests red-first. Fresh focused result: 1 file passed, 12 tests passed; control-room typecheck exit 0.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red: write the failing spec for the shared surface-audit predicates. Each predicate must be asserted to be non-vacuous and to detect a real violation, using small hand-built DOM fragments plus at least one real rendered surface. Cover: auditFactChips (section 12 bar 3) flags a cr.fact.* wrapper with no cr.chip.* descendant and reports the offending fact id; auditActionLegality (bar 4) flags an enabled cr.action.* whose data-command-id is absent from the supplied nextAllowedCommands, and does NOT flag a disabled one; auditKeyboardReachability flags an interactive cr.action.* that is unreachable (negative tabindex, aria-hidden, or hidden) and confirms DOM order matches visual order; auditLiveRegions (section 11.1) flags a cr.banner.* carrying neither role=status/alert nor aria-live; auditActionParity (section 4.16 last clause) flags any cr.action.* test id present at wide width but missing at narrow. Every predicate returns a checked count, and every test asserts checked is greater than zero, so an audit that swept nothing fails instead of passing. Tests fail because the module does not exist yet.
implementationPlan.note: TDD RED recorded for five non-vacuous production audit surfaces. Tests pin exact offending ids and stable codes, include enabled/disabled/supplied command cases, all three unreachable shapes, explicit DOM/visual-order agreement and mismatch, live-region semantics, wide/narrow action parity, a real rendered Fact, and the POL actor-badge exclusion. implementationPlan.description: Make step 4 green. implementationPlan.note: GREEN: implemented five frozen-result audit predicates in 122 production lines. Exact reserved-prefix selectors count every swept fact/action/banner; action legality only compares enabled controls against supplied NextAllowedCommand ids; keyboard audit catches hidden/aria-hidden/negative-tab and CSS-order mismatch while tolerating disabled controls; live regions and wide/narrow parity return exact offending test ids and stable codes. implementationPlan.description: Add the CR-A11Y-001 monochrome predicate, red first then green, in the same two files. Export auditTruthClassMonochrome, which calls describeTruthClass from @moe/control-room-model for all five classes and asserts the (glyph, shortLabel, borderStyle) tuple is pairwise distinct with semanticTone deliberately excluded from the comparison. It must call the production function, never carry its own copy of the descriptors, or the property is asserted against a reimplementation instead of the real surface. It must assert it examined exactly five classes, so a shortened input list cannot pass. Note in a comment why border alone is insufficient: four classes are solid and only UNKNOWN is dashed, so the tuple carries the distinction, not the border. The test must also confirm the predicate is sensitive: feed it two descriptors made identical except for semanticTone and assert it reports a collision with a stable code.
implementationPlan.note: TDD red then green: auditTruthClassMonochrome now obtains the five descriptors from production describeTruthClass, requires exactly five, and detects pairwise (glyph, shortLabel, borderStyle) collisions while deliberately excluding semanticTone; border-only insufficiency is documented. AMENDED 2026-08-09 by governor-f70d1157 — OWNERSHIP WIDENED BY ONE PRODUCTION FILE.

Your audit found a real bar-4 defect and you were right to refuse to weaken it. Fix the production code instead. `apps/control-room/src/approvals/approval-inbox.tsx` and its existing focused tests are now ADDED to this step's affected paths, alongside `apps/control-room/src/a11y/ui-wide-acceptance.test.tsx`.

THE DEFECT, as you measured it: `DecisionControl` renders enabled `cr.action.*` buttons with no `data-command-id`. Because all four approval detail surfaces reuse that component, the audit correctly returns ACTION_WITHOUT_COMMAND on 7 controls — plan approve/reject, expansion approve/decline, acceptance accept/decline, and cutover activate — with focused acceptance at 20 passed / 4 failed.

THE FIX, and nothing beyond it: give `DecisionControl` the `data-command-id` its callers already supply, so each rendered control carries the command id it will actually issue. Do NOT invent a command id, do NOT derive one, and do NOT default one when a caller supplies none — the id must come from the caller's supplied command, because a fabricated id would make the audit pass while the control still cannot be checked against nextAllowedCommands. If a call site turns out not to supply a command at all, that is a second defect: report it, do not paper over it.

DO NOT weaken the audit. `auditActionLegality` stays exactly as written — it is correct and it just proved its worth. The four failing cases must go green because the production code was fixed, never because the predicate was relaxed.

SCOPE LIMIT: this amendment adds one component file plus its existing tests. If the fix cannot be made within that boundary — for example if it requires changing a call site outside approval-inbox.tsx, or a shared type — report blocked rather than widening further on your own authority. You will not be penalised for a second block here; you have already been right twice today.

Commit by explicit pathspec over exactly your owned paths, and re-run the focused acceptance to confirm 24/24 before completing the step.

QA FULL VERIFICATION RECORD (approval summary capped at 2000 chars; long form here).

amend-1 SCOPE — HONOURED EXACTLY, AND I CHECKED THE BOUNDARY THE GOVERNOR DREW, NOT JUST THE FIX.
The whole of `approval-inbox.tsx`'s change is one added line plus a stray blank-line removal:
`data-command-id={control.commandId ?? undefined}` at line 80.
No call site outside `approval-inbox.tsx`. No shared type touched. `git diff` over the amendment window shows the approvals directory otherwise untouched.

PROVENANCE OF THE ID — the governor's specific concern, and it holds. The value comes from `control.commandId`, the caller's supplied command. Nothing invents, derives, or defaults one. The `enabled` guard at line 76 is `control.state === "ENABLED" && control.commandId !== null`, so a control with no command renders DISABLED rather than acquiring a fabricated id — which is the correct shape, since `auditActionLegality` only inspects non-disabled actions. Both directions are pinned in `approval-inbox.test.tsx`: line 226 asserts the rendered button's `data-command-id` equals the exact caller-supplied id; lines 231-237 assert a `commandId: null` control renders with the attribute ABSENT. A fabricated-id implementation fails the second test.

`auditActionLegality` IS BYTE-UNCHANGED. `git diff 588a0f6 0075790 -- surface-audit.ts` returns exactly one hunk, and it is not in that function. The four ACTION_WITHOUT_COMMAND cases went green because production was fixed, never because the predicate moved. That was the governor's stated rejection condition and it is not met.

THE ONE AUDIT CHANGE, INVESTIGATED RATHER THAN WAVED THROUGH. `visualOrderMismatches` now filters to non-disabled actions before comparing DOM order to visual order. I treated this as a possible relaxation and checked it three ways:
1. It is in `auditKeyboardReachability`, not `auditActionLegality`, so it is not the mechanism for the amendment's green.
2. It is a CONSISTENCY fix, not a weakening: `isUnreachable` already returns false for disabled actions (surface-audit.ts:99), so the audit had already declared them out of scope for reachability while the order path contradicted that. The change makes the two agree.
3. MY OWN MUTATION DRILL, not the worker's. I reverted the filter to `const interactive = actions;` and ran the focused suite: RED, 1 failed / 10 passed, failing exactly `surface-audit.test.ts:139` — "ignores informational action metadata when comparing interactive order". The new test is load-bearing. Restored from the captured blob and verified `git hash-object` == `b97e8b982fd1758be87d92a9e7f4a4f9a8f07a10`, the pre-drill value — NOT `git status`, and NOT `git checkout HEAD --`, per the practice established on this board an hour ago.

DoD 1 — MET. Keyboard: CR-A11Y-002 completes J1's three human actions via `userEvent.keyboard` only, including board h/l column traversal, with the human-action count asserted <= 3. Colour: five truth chips proven distinct by (glyph, shortlabel, border) tuple — `classes.size === 5` and `tuples.size === 5` — plus production `auditTruthClassMonochrome()` returning `{checked: 5, violations: []}`. `auditKeyboardReachability` and `auditActionParity` run over every canonical surface at 1280 and 640.

DoD 2 — FIRST HALF MET, SECOND HALF DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE. Loading/degraded: parameterised per-surface sweeps assert degraded truth stays stale (`[data-testid$='.asof']` present) and that both degraded and loading states keep every enabled action command-authorised; a fixture missing its renderer THROWS rather than silently skipping. Timing (server/stream/render/human): see the escalation note below.

DoD 3 — MET, against the bars the spec actually specifies. Section 12 line 742 of the pinned spec names four global bars: (1) J1 <= 3 human actions; (2) one fan-out proposal <= 1 approval; (3) every `cr.fact.*` has a `cr.chip.*` descendant; (4) every enabled `cr.action.*` originates from `nextAllowedCommands`. Bar 1 asserted in CR-A11Y-002. Bar 2 recorded as explicitly NOT APPLICABLE with its reason (CR-J1-002 forbids mounting `cr.graph.*` in this slice) plus a positive assertion that zero `cr.graph.*` elements mount — recorded as N/A rather than passed as an empty sweep, which is what the plan required. Bar 3 via `auditFactChips`. Bar 4 via `auditActionLegality` — the bar that caught the real defect. `prefers-reduced-motion` (spec line 686) and table reflow (line 432) are section 4/10 styling requirements, NOT section 12 bars; step 10 disclosed them as adjacent non-coverage and I do not score them against DoD 3.

DoD 4 — MET. 28 files / 421 tests, exit 0, re-run twice.

NON-VACUITY, checked structurally rather than by counting greens. Every audit call goes through `expectCleanAudit`, which asserts `checked > 0` BEFORE `violations: []`, so a sweep that inspected nothing cannot pass. The surface list is asserted non-empty, set-equal to a hand-written `EXPECTED_SURFACES`, and duplicate-free.

Same infra fault the board escalated today. `0075790` is this worker's own explicit-pathspec commit. Not scored against them.

planningNotes.risks:
1. VACUOUS SWEEP is the primary failure mode here and project rail 1 names it explicitly: a surface audit that finds zero facts, zero actions, or zero chips PASSES while testing nothing. Every audit must return a `checked` count and every acceptance test must assert `checked` is greater than zero before asserting zero violations.

2. GLOBAL ROUTER HIJACK. j/k/h/l/Enter/p/Esc are already surface-local. A global listener that also claims them will double-handle, and a global `a` or `/` binding will fire while the operator is typing in cr.goals.form. The router must own ONLY the bindings no surface owns (g-chord, a, /, ?, [, ]) and must refuse with a stable reason code when focus is in a text entry or when the event already originated inside a surface handler.

3. REASON CODES, not booleans. Epic rail 6 and project rail 1: every refusal path in the resolver returns a specific stable code and the test asserts THAT code. A test asserting only 'did not navigate' is one added guard away from vacuous.

4. ASSERT AGAINST PRODUCTION. auditMonochrome must call describeTruthClass from @moe/control-room-model. If it carries its own copy of the five descriptors, the test proves only that the copy is self-consistent.

5. PREFIX INVARIANT. Adding any element whose test id starts with cr.fact. or cr.chip. that is not a real fact wrapper or chip silently corrupts bar 3 for every surface. The skip-link and help overlay must not use those prefixes.

6. SPEC 4.16 LAYOUT IS NOT IN THIS TASK. Only its last clause ('nothing is desktop-only: every action available wide is available narrow') is a structural invariant assertable without layout work. The actual reflow (nav rail collapses to icons, inspector becomes an overlay sheet, sticky board headers, pinned decision buttons, two-line tables) is unimplemented and needs its own task. Do not half-build it here.

7. prefers-reduced-motion (section 11.1) is also unimplemented and is NOT covered by this plan's DoD. jsdom does not implement matchMedia by default, so it needs a deliberate shim; flag it rather than smuggling it in.

8. Bar 2 (one fan-out proposal costs at most one approval) is NOT applicable to the committed surfaces: the graph projection renders GraphPlaceholder in this slice and CR-J1-002 requires cr.graph.* never mount. State that in the harness as an explicit not-applicable with a reason, never as a passing assertion over zero cases.

9. File size: if surface-audit.ts approaches 250 lines, split the truth/monochrome predicate into a sibling module rather than letting it grow. Same for the acceptance test file.
